A photonic wall pressure sensor for fluid mechanics applications
top_cited_works.abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a micro-optical wall pressure sensor concept based on the optical modes of dielectric resonators. The sensing element is a spherical micro-resonator with a diameter of a few hundred micrometers. A latex membrane that is flush mounted on the wall transmits the normal pressure to the sensing element. Changes in the wall pressure perturb the sphere's morphology, leading to a shift in the optical modes. The wall pressure is measured by monitoring the shifts in the optical modes. Prototype sensors with polydimethylsiloxane micro-spheres are tested in a steady two-dimensional channel flow and in a plane wave acoustic tube. Results indicate sensor resolutions of ∼20 mPa and bandwidth of up to 2 kHz.

recent_works.title: UAV-Based Optical Fiber Sensor System for Remote Detection of Hazardous Gases in Emergency Situations
recent_works.abstract: Abstract This study presents a drone-integrated optical fiber sensor deployment and retraction system for the remote detection of hazardous gases in hard-to-reach or high-risk environments. The system consists of four optical fibers, each coated with a distinct microporous material engineered to selectively detect hazardous gases. This method ensures precise, real-time detection with high sensitivity at ambient temperatures. A key innovation of the system is its custom-designed deployment and retraction mechanism, which allows controlled extrusion of the sensing fibers during flight. The mechanism uses a low-RPM, high-torque motor controlled by an ESP32 microcontroller and motor driver, all mounted on the drone in a weight-balanced configuration to preserve flight stability. Bluetooth communication enables wireless command of deployment sequences via a mobile device. Unlike conventional sensors, this system requires no elevated temperatures or exposed electronics at the sensing site, improving safety and adaptability. The drone’s mobility, combined with the optical system’s low power consumption and multiplexing capability, makes it a versatile tool for environmental monitoring,...

recent_works.title: Hazardous Gas Sensing Technologies: A Review of Chemiresistive, Electrochemical, and Optical Fiber Sensors with a Vision for UAV-Based Emergency Response
recent_works.abstract: Hazardous gases such as ammonia$\left(\mathbf{N H}_{3}\right)$, chlorine$\left(\text{Cl}_{2}\right)$, hydrogen sulfide$\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{S}\right)$, and sulfur dioxide$\left(\text{SO}_{2}\right)$pose serious health risks during industrial accidents, chemical spills, and emergency events. First responders are often the most vulnerable during such situations due to limited early detection capabilities. This review presents recent advancements in hazardous gas sensor technologies. The paper covers three major sensor types: chemiresistive, electrochemical, and optical fiber-based sensors. Key developments in sensing materials, detection limits, response times, and environmental durability are discussed. The authors also highlight an ongoing effort to develop a UAV-based gas sensing platform that utilizes a four-channel Long Period Fiber Grating (LPFG) array coated with$\text{SnO}_{2}, \text{ZnO}, \text{Pf}$, and Pt for selective gas detection.

recent_works.title: Introducing CFD Concepts in an Applied Fluid Mechanics Course
recent_works.abstract: The use of computational fluid dynamics in engineering technology courses result in many challenges due to the lack of differential equations knowledge.However, CFD is usually useful for technology students during their capstone design, especially when dealing with fluid components design such as valves, sprinkler systems, heat exchangers.Most of the time, instructors just show one or two slides about the existence of CFD in their fluid mechanics courses without providing further information.Some programs introduced a finite element analysis standalone course into their curriculum, seeing the necessity for the students to grasp the core concept applied to structural analysis.Some mechanical engineering programs introduce CFD use in their courses, but students have differential equation knowledge.In this paper, CFD is introduced to junior students in their applied fluid mechanics class through a laboratory activity.The course is taught as a part of the Mechanical Engineering Technology program at the University of North Texas.

recent_works.title: Identifying Industry-Preferred Automation Software in Engineering: An Indeed-Based Analysis to Inform Engineering Technology Curriculum Design
recent_works.abstract: In the evolving field of automation engineering, staying aligned with industry software demands is critical to preparing graduates for the modern workforce. This study investigates the prevalence of leading industrial automation platforms—Rockwell / Allen-Bradley (RSLogix / Studio 5000), Siemens (TIA Portal / Step 7), and Schneider Electric (EcoStruxure / Unity Pro)—across job postings collected from Indeed using the keyword "automation engineering." The research compiles a structured dataset of job postings with seven fields: ID, Job Title, Organization, Rockwell / Allen-Bradley, Siemens, Schneider Electric, and Posting URL. Each entry is manually coded to indicate whether the listed software platforms are mentioned, allowing for frequency analysis and comparative evaluation. Preliminary insights suggest that while all three platforms have broad relevance, employer preference may vary significantly by region, sector, and job role.
